symbols.name: authentication
symbols.signature: export declare const authentication: (config: IRpcAuthenticationConfig) => IRpcPlugin;
symbols.purpose: Installs original per-frame protection, actual physical-session binding and replay checks; encryption runs before signing, verification before decryption.
symbols.core:
config: Application configuration documented by IRpcAuthenticationConfig; factory returns a definition, installation occurs in createEndpoint middlewares.
Immutable IRpcPlugin definition; unsupported or unreadable fields fail the original installation with INVALID_CONFIG and retained cause.
encrypt: Outbound sync/async encryption runs after the endpoint wraps its encoded value with replay metadata and before signing. Throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with its cause.
encrypt.value: Replay-bound authentication envelope produced by the endpoint, including its encoded payload; not the bare application payload.
encrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Encrypted value or its Promise, passed unchanged into sign.
Leave encrypt and decrypt out together when messages need signatures but not encryption. In that case, sign receives the unencrypted authentication envelope: the message data together with the information used to detect replay. Omitting encryption does not remove signing or verification.
Configure `encrypt` with `decrypt` for confidentiality and `sign` with `verify` for integrity; `encodedType` names the actual protected representation.
decrypt: Inbound sync/async decryption runs on the value recovered by verify. The endpoint then validates the recovered authentication envelope and replay binding.
decrypt.value: Verified protected value returned by verify.
decrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Recovered replay-bound authentication envelope or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with the original cause.
Omit decrypt only when encrypt is also omitted. After verify checks the signature and recovers the inner value, the endpoint directly checks that value as the authentication envelope, including its replay information. It does not try to decrypt the value.
sign: Outbound sync/async signing runs after optional encryption and returns the complete protected frame representation. Signing and verification are required even without encryption.
sign.value: Encrypted value when encrypt exists, otherwise the replay-bound authentication envelope.
sign.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Signed representation or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Keep the declared encodedType output domain.
There is no default signing function. Provide sign together with verify whenever authentication is enabled. This remains required when encrypt and decrypt are configured: encryption alone is insufficient, and omitting sign rejects the configuration.
verify: Inbound sync/async verification receives the protected frame and must recover its authenticated inner value; returning a boolean is not a verification verdict protocol.
verify.value: Protected value received at the authentication pipeline edge.
verify.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.

examples:
import { connect, createEndpoint } from '@migaia/rpc-core'
import { createMemoryTransportPair } from '@migaia/rpc-core/adapters/memory'

const [left, right] = createMemoryTransportPair()
const server = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'server',
  transport: right,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: right })]
})
server.provide('double', (context) => context.success((context.data as number) * 2))
const client = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'client',
  targetIds: ['server'],
  transport: left,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: left })]
})
console.log(await client.send<number>('server', 'double', 21))
await client.dispose()
await server.dispose()
left.close()

import { connect, createEndpoint } from '@migaia/rpc-core'
import { createMemoryTransportPair } from '@migaia/rpc-core/adapters/memory'

const [left, right] = createMemoryTransportPair()
const endpoint = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'local',
  transport: left,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: left })]
})
await endpoint.dispose()
console.log(left.closed, right.closed)
left.close()
console.log(left.closed, right.closed)

symbols.name: createEndpoint
symbols.signature: export declare const createEndpoint: IPublicCallable;
symbols.purpose:
Creates the full canonical endpoint with provider, outbound, discovery and control roots; actual middleware tuple narrows optional ping/manual controls.

The examples use application-chosen id values and a caller-created memory transport pair. Both transport and connect({ transport }) refer to the same side; memory options default to {}, with asynchronous delivery and no value cloning. middlewares is the required installation tuple; targetIds is an optional application seed list, default []. provide registers an application method whose context.data is the request and context.success(value) forms its reply. send(targetId, method, data, options?) takes the target and method named by that application; options defaults to {}. Dispose each endpoint, then close the borrowed pair as its creator.
symbols.core:
config: Application IRpcFactoryConfig whose actual protocol/codec/framer/transport types satisfy both directed pipeline edges; middlewares is the actual finite installation tuple.
Promise of the selected endpoint surface; invalid inputs fail before publication, failed construction rolls back and preserves original/cleanup causes. An unclassified middleware install failure gains CALLBACK_FAILED without replacing mutable native type/stack; foreign semantic identities stay intact and immutable values remain on cause.
provide: Registers one provider for a unique method name; duplicate registration throws PROVIDER_DUPLICATED.
provide.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
provide.provider: Application callback receives IRpcContext and returns context.success or context.failed synchronously or asynchronously. Legacy ordinary throws usually become INTERNAL; trusted wire summaries and SCHEMA_INVALID retain public classification. Runtime operations serialize the original failure.
The same endpoint for chaining; disposal rejects new registrations.
on: Registers a one-way event listener; callbacks receive IRpcContext and async failures are observed through endpoint hooks.
on.event: Application event name matching the sender dispatch method.
on.listener: Application callback receives IRpcContext, returns void or Promise<void>, and should not retain expired response operations.
Idempotent unsubscriber removes only this registration.
send: Sends a correlated scalar request to the selected receiver and waits for one actual provider result.
send.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
send.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
send.data: Application request payload validated by the installed contract/codec.
send.options: Optional ISendOptions supplied by the caller; timeout, cancellation, transfer, idempotency and trace remain explicit.
Promise of provider data; remote business failure, cancellation, deadline, transport or lifecycle failure rejects with its native coded error. A synchronous UUID admission failure releases operation signal listeners; ordinary send cancellation keeps RpcAbortError.
sendAll: Sends the same scalar method to the statically configured target seeds and keeps each target success/failure separately.
sendAll.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
sendAll.data: Application payload sent independently to every selected target.
sendAll.options: Caller ISendOptions applied to the selected fan-out operations.
IRpcFanoutResult maps receiver/target keys to fulfilled data or original rejected errors.
dispatch: Sends a legacy one-way event without awaiting business completion; pair with on on the receiving endpoint.
dispatch.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
dispatch.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
dispatch.data: Application event payload for the receiving listener.
Returns void once dispatch is initiated; failures are contained in endpoint hooks.
dispatchAll: Dispatches one event to the statically configured target seeds without waiting for business listeners.
dispatchAll.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
dispatchAll.data: Application event payload for each selected target.
Returns void after scheduling selected dispatches; hooks observe failures.
group: Reserves every request-only step before execution, then runs in order until first failure; successful earlier effects are not rolled back.
group.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
group.steps: Application nonempty method/payload array admitted as IRpcRuntimeGroupSteps.
group.options: Optional IRpcRuntimeGroupOptions with actual ordering/cancellation/idempotency and local send controls.
Promise of actual step outcomes; unsupported native group capability rejects before dispatch.
outcome: Reads an original logical key outcome from the provider store without executing providers again.
outcome.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
outcome.idempotencyKey: Original application-issued key used for the same earlier logical operation.
IRpcRuntimeOutcomeResult reports pending/done/unknown and store continuity; unknown never proves nonexecution.
announceClose: Announces a bounded drain window to one peer while leaving actual physical close with its owning adapter.
announceClose.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
announceClose.options: Caller drainMs duration and optional receiverId from discovery; this is a relative peer announcement.
Resolves when the close control is sent; it does not await remote resource disposal.
ping: Checks one actual receiver liveness; requires installed ping capability and actual negotiated support.
ping.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
ping.receiverId: Specific receiver identifier returned by discovery candidates or connect.getServerList; never invent an instance address.
ping.options: Optional IRpcPingOptions with local signal and deadline override.
Promise<boolean> for the observed reply; disposal settles an active ping as false. Calling after disposal or without ping capability throws its coded error. Ping cancellation does not require abort middleware.
pingAll: Checks liveness of the statically configured target seeds and retains individual success/failure results.
IRpcFanoutResult<boolean> keyed by the selected actual receivers.
connect: Connection/discovery controls derived from the actual middleware tuple; manual mode exposes query and registration operations.
discovery: Read-only candidate listing and explicit receiver pin controls sharing the canonical discovery owner.
hooks: Local diagnostic subscription facade; hooks.on receives IRpcHookEvent and returns an unsubscriber.
dispose: Idempotently stops admission, drains owned work and releases middleware/adapter resources in the canonical lifecycle order.
Promise resolves after disposal; cleanup failures remain reachable through standard cause/errors traversal, including all failures in the same batch; future operations fail ENDPOINT_DISPOSED.
id: Application-assigned stable local endpoint identifier included in outgoing routes.
scheduler: Application monotonic IScheduler shared by endpoint deadlines and PluginHost; now must be finite nonnegative milliseconds.
systemScheduler uses host monotonic time and timers.
Pass the application’s monotonic scheduler when endpoint deadlines must share its clock. Omit it to use the host scheduler.
wallClock: Application IWallClock supplies only wire sentAt and hook timestamps as nonnegative safe-integer epoch milliseconds.
systemWallClock uses the host epoch clock.
Set a wall clock when wire timestamps and diagnostic timestamps must use the application clock. It does not control deadlines.
transport: Actual application adapter selected by top-level config or native connect middleware; native source evidence remains adapter-owned.
Absent: use the selected connect middleware transport; otherwise construction fails.
Supply the exact original carrier side owned by this caller; choose a transport factory for the supported host.
protocol: Canonical semantic IRpcProtocol descriptor selected independently of codec encoding.
rpcProtocolV1 is the default canonical protocol.
Use the protocol descriptor agreed by both ends. Omit it for Core’s default protocol.
codec: ICodec from @migaia/serialize/codec whose encoded output exactly matches the selected framer input.
identityCodecV1 preserves the canonical semantic envelope.
Use a codec whose output matches the framer input. Both ends must agree on the encoded representation.
framer: IRpcFramer from rpc-contract/framing whose actual output is accepted by the selected transport.
messageFramerV1 uses complete unfragmented messages.
Use the framer agreed by both ends; its output must match the transport’s accepted frame.
targetIds: Optional known-peer base identifiers from application deployment configuration; automatic discovery can resolve more later.
Empty seed list; discovery remains available.
provider: Application map of unique method names to IRpcProvider callbacks installed before endpoint construction returns.
Absent: register providers later through provide.
Register startup handlers here when they must exist before ingress starts. Later registrations can use provide on a provider-capable endpoint.
providerLimits: Optional IRpcProviderLimits applied to the existing shared execution/replay admission owner.
Global 256, per-peer 64, replay per-peer 1024.
Bound active provider work when expensive operations need backpressure. The defaults are 256 global and 64 per peer.
idempotency: Optional actual original result store and authenticated scope function for keyed provider work.
Absent: use the endpoint-owned canonical keyed replay policy.
Provide an outcome store on the serving endpoint when retries carry the same idempotency key. A shared store also needs a session scope.
idempotency.store: Optional caller-held IRpcIdempotencyStore shared only across actual intended sessions.
Absent: use the original endpoint-local store.
idempotency.scope: Synchronous application callback receives actual admitted token and senderId, returns a stable scope string; it must not treat arbitrary wire claims as identity.
Absent: canonical admitted-session scope is used.
Derive isolation from an admitted token when sharing an outcome store across sessions.
replay: Outbound active identifiers plus settled tombstone retention, separate from business result storage.
Use maxEntries 4096 and ttlMs 310000.
Size retained outbound identifiers for the request rate and replay window. This ledger is separate from the keyed business-result store.
replay.maxEntries: Maximum retained outbound request identities including active operations and settled tombstones.
`4096` retained outbound identities.
replay.ttlMs: Scheduler milliseconds to retain settled outbound request identity tombstones.
`310000` milliseconds after settlement.
middlewares: Required ordered finite tuple of actual middleware definitions installed atomically by PluginHost.
features: Optional finite immutable tuple of actual native IRpcFeature roots; dependencies remain private and only selected public surfaces are projected.
Empty tuple adds no user-defined features.
Install application features when endpoint-owned cleanup should release them. Omit this tuple when no extra feature is needed.
construction: Caller construction cancellation/deadline; failure still rolls back every installed middleware in original lifecycle order.
Absent: no caller abort or construction deadline.
construction.signal: Optional caller cancellation signal controlling construction and its complete rollback.
Absent: construction has an uncancelled native signal.
construction.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative construction deadline or false to disable; rollback retains the primary failure and cleanup failures.
Absent or false: no construction deadline.
Disable only the construction deadline.
Use false to rely solely on caller cancellation; use a finite budget when construction must finish within a deadline.
symbols.advanced: Compose actual endpoint or runtime peers while keeping transport and lifecycle ownership with their canonical owners.
parameters: config: TConfig & IChecked<TConfig>
config: ILegacyDefault<TTargetId, TMiddlewares, TFeatures>
symbols.returns: Promise<IRecursiveProvideSurface<IFullEndpointSurface<ITarget<TConfig>, IFactoryDiscoveryMode<IMiddlewares<TConfig>>, IFactoryPingCapability<IMiddlewares<TConfig>>, IMiddlewares<TConfig>, IFeatures<TConfig>> & TAdditionalSurface>> | Promise<IRecursiveProvideSurface<IFullEndpointSurface<TTargetId, IFactoryDiscoveryMode<TMiddlewares>, IFactoryPingCapability<TMiddlewares>, TMiddlewares, TFeatures> & TAdditionalSurface>>
examples:
import { connect, createEndpoint } from '@migaia/rpc-core'
import { createMemoryTransportPair } from '@migaia/rpc-core/adapters/memory'

const [left, right] = createMemoryTransportPair()
const server = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'server',
  transport: right,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: right })]
})
server.provide('double', (context) => context.success((context.data as number) * 2))
const client = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'client',
  targetIds: ['server'],
  transport: left,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: left })]
})
console.log(await client.send<number>('server', 'double', 21))
await client.dispose()
await server.dispose()
left.close()

import { connect, createEndpoint } from '@migaia/rpc-core'
import { createMemoryTransportPair } from '@migaia/rpc-core/adapters/memory'

const [left, right] = createMemoryTransportPair()
const endpoint = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'local',
  transport: left,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: left })]
})
await endpoint.dispose()
console.log(left.closed, right.closed)
left.close()
console.log(left.closed, right.closed)

isRpcErrorInstance / isRpcRemoteError / isRpcTimeoutError 按稳定字段跨 realm/副本判断，不能依赖 instanceof；isRpcError 只检查字符串 code，不能替代错误族守卫。RpcError、RpcRemoteError、RpcTimeoutError 等仅类型导出，唯一公开可构造类为 RpcLifecycleError，供持有自身释放状态的消费方使用。

symbols.purpose: Installs original per-frame protection, actual physical-session binding and replay checks; encryption runs before signing, verification before decryption.
symbols.core:
encrypt: Outbound sync/async encryption runs after the endpoint wraps its encoded value with replay metadata and before signing. Throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with its cause.
encrypt.value: Replay-bound authentication envelope produced by the endpoint, including its encoded payload; not the bare application payload.
encrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Encrypted value or its Promise, passed unchanged into sign.
Leave encrypt and decrypt out together when messages need signatures but not encryption. In that case, sign receives the unencrypted authentication envelope: the message data together with the information used to detect replay. Omitting encryption does not remove signing or verification.
Configure `encrypt` with `decrypt` for confidentiality and `sign` with `verify` for integrity; `encodedType` names the actual protected representation.
decrypt: Inbound sync/async decryption runs on the value recovered by verify. The endpoint then validates the recovered authentication envelope and replay binding.
decrypt.value: Verified protected value returned by verify.
decrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Recovered replay-bound authentication envelope or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with the original cause.
Omit decrypt only when encrypt is also omitted. After verify checks the signature and recovers the inner value, the endpoint directly checks that value as the authentication envelope, including its replay information. It does not try to decrypt the value.
sign: Outbound sync/async signing runs after optional encryption and returns the complete protected frame representation. Signing and verification are required even without encryption.
sign.value: Encrypted value when encrypt exists, otherwise the replay-bound authentication envelope.
sign.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Signed representation or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Keep the declared encodedType output domain.
There is no default signing function. Provide sign together with verify whenever authentication is enabled. This remains required when encrypt and decrypt are configured: encryption alone is insufficient, and omitting sign rejects the configuration.
verify: Inbound sync/async verification receives the protected frame and must recover its authenticated inner value; returning a boolean is not a verification verdict protocol.
verify.value: Protected value received at the authentication pipeline edge.
verify.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Authenticated inner value or its Promise, passed to decrypt when configured; reject or throw on invalid signatures. Local reporting retains the original verification failure, which may be sensitive; the peer receives a sanitized summary. Other returned values still undergo envelope/replay validation.

encodedType: Declared protected-output domain must match the next physical pipeline edge. Encrypt/decrypt and sign/verify are complete pairs, at least signing is required, and encryption additionally requires signing.
any: do not impose a declared protected-output value category.

localEndpointId: Serving endpoint identifier provided by the actual provider execution context.
callerGeneration: Optional caller generation from an actually admitted generation-aware directory task.
targetGeneration: Exact accepted provider execution/session generation, never a launch-attempt counter.
data: Application data provided by the actual request, event, schema or result owner.
signal: Provider-owned AbortSignal from the admitted execution scope; deadline, caller cancellation and endpoint disposal can retire this lifetime independently of outbound abort middleware.
senderId: Direct authenticated sender identifier provided by the actual admitted inbound binding.
route: Optional ordered signed forwarding node identifiers; originating ordinary calls omit it.
trace: Optional caller-issued opaque diagnostic trace; downstream calls must pass it explicitly.

timeoutMs: Remaining actual provider deadline derived from the original endpoint monotonic clock; absent without a deadline.
success: Constructs explicit successful completion while this provider lifetime is active.
success.data: Optional application success data, omitted only when actually undefined.
success.options: Optional explicit original transfer list for physical result ownership.

failed: Constructs explicit application failure without replacing it with an internal exception.

failed.code: Application-owned stable semantic failure code.

dispatchTo: Issues a provider-scoped one-way dispatch using the original provider execution owner.
dispatchTo.input: Application method/data and optional explicitly chosen target id; original execution controls validate its route.
Returns void after dispatch initiation; provider lifecycle and endpoint hooks contain later failures.

provide: Registers one provider for a unique method name; duplicate registration throws PROVIDER_DUPLICATED.
provide.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
provide.provider: Application callback receives IRpcContext and returns context.success or context.failed synchronously or asynchronously. Legacy ordinary throws usually become INTERNAL; trusted wire summaries and SCHEMA_INVALID retain public classification. Runtime operations serialize the original failure.
The same endpoint for chaining; disposal rejects new registrations.
on: Registers a one-way event listener; callbacks receive IRpcContext and async failures are observed through endpoint hooks.
on.event: Application event name matching the sender dispatch method.
on.listener: Application callback receives IRpcContext, returns void or Promise<void>, and should not retain expired response operations.
Idempotent unsubscriber removes only this registration.
send: Sends a correlated scalar request to the selected receiver and waits for one actual provider result.
send.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
send.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
send.data: Application request payload validated by the installed contract/codec.
send.options: Optional ISendOptions supplied by the caller; timeout, cancellation, transfer, idempotency and trace remain explicit.
Promise of provider data; remote business failure, cancellation, deadline, transport or lifecycle failure rejects with its native coded error. A synchronous UUID admission failure releases operation signal listeners; ordinary send cancellation keeps RpcAbortError.
sendAll: Sends the same scalar method to the statically configured target seeds and keeps each target success/failure separately.
sendAll.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
sendAll.data: Application payload sent independently to every selected target.
sendAll.options: Caller ISendOptions applied to the selected fan-out operations.
IRpcFanoutResult maps receiver/target keys to fulfilled data or original rejected errors.
dispatch: Sends a legacy one-way event without awaiting business completion; pair with on on the receiving endpoint.
dispatch.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
dispatch.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
dispatch.data: Application event payload for the receiving listener.
Returns void once dispatch is initiated; failures are contained in endpoint hooks.
dispatchAll: Dispatches one event to the statically configured target seeds without waiting for business listeners.
dispatchAll.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
dispatchAll.data: Application event payload for each selected target.
Returns void after scheduling selected dispatches; hooks observe failures.
group: Reserves every request-only step before execution, then runs in order until first failure; successful earlier effects are not rolled back.
group.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
group.steps: Application nonempty method/payload array admitted as IRpcRuntimeGroupSteps.
group.options: Optional IRpcRuntimeGroupOptions with actual ordering/cancellation/idempotency and local send controls.
Promise of actual step outcomes; unsupported native group capability rejects before dispatch.
outcome: Reads an original logical key outcome from the provider store without executing providers again.
outcome.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
outcome.idempotencyKey: Original application-issued key used for the same earlier logical operation.
IRpcRuntimeOutcomeResult reports pending/done/unknown and store continuity; unknown never proves nonexecution.
announceClose: Announces a bounded drain window to one peer while leaving actual physical close with its owning adapter.
announceClose.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
announceClose.options: Caller drainMs duration and optional receiverId from discovery; this is a relative peer announcement.
Resolves when the close control is sent; it does not await remote resource disposal.
ping: Checks one actual receiver liveness; requires installed ping capability and actual negotiated support.
ping.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
ping.receiverId: Specific receiver identifier returned by discovery candidates or connect.getServerList; never invent an instance address.
ping.options: Optional IRpcPingOptions with local signal and deadline override.
Promise<boolean> for the observed reply; disposal settles an active ping as false. Calling after disposal or without ping capability throws its coded error. Ping cancellation does not require abort middleware.
pingAll: Checks liveness of the statically configured target seeds and retains individual success/failure results.
IRpcFanoutResult<boolean> keyed by the selected actual receivers.
connect: Connection/discovery controls derived from the actual middleware tuple; manual mode exposes query and registration operations.
discovery: Read-only candidate listing and explicit receiver pin controls sharing the canonical discovery owner.
hooks: Local diagnostic subscription facade; hooks.on receives IRpcHookEvent and returns an unsubscriber.
dispose: Idempotently stops admission, drains owned work and releases middleware/adapter resources in the canonical lifecycle order.
Promise resolves after disposal; cleanup failures remain reachable through standard cause/errors traversal, including all failures in the same batch; future operations fail ENDPOINT_DISPOSED.

id: Application-assigned stable local endpoint identifier included in outgoing routes.
scheduler: Application monotonic IScheduler shared by endpoint deadlines and PluginHost; now must be finite nonnegative milliseconds.
systemScheduler uses host monotonic time and timers.

wallClock: Application IWallClock supplies only wire sentAt and hook timestamps as nonnegative safe-integer epoch milliseconds.
systemWallClock uses the host epoch clock.

transport: Actual application adapter selected by top-level config or native connect middleware; native source evidence remains adapter-owned.
Absent: use the selected connect middleware transport; otherwise construction fails.

protocol: Canonical semantic IRpcProtocol descriptor selected independently of codec encoding.
rpcProtocolV1 is the default canonical protocol.

codec: ICodec from @migaia/serialize/codec whose encoded output exactly matches the selected framer input.
identityCodecV1 preserves the canonical semantic envelope.

framer: IRpcFramer from rpc-contract/framing whose actual output is accepted by the selected transport.

targetIds: Optional known-peer base identifiers from application deployment configuration; automatic discovery can resolve more later.

provider: Application map of unique method names to IRpcProvider callbacks installed before endpoint construction returns.
Absent: register providers later through provide.

providerLimits: Optional IRpcProviderLimits applied to the existing shared execution/replay admission owner.
Global 256, per-peer 64, replay per-peer 1024.

idempotency: Optional actual original result store and authenticated scope function for keyed provider work.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
id: Application-assigned stable local endpoint identifier included in outgoing routes.
scheduler: Application monotonic IScheduler shared by endpoint deadlines and PluginHost; now must be finite nonnegative milliseconds.
systemScheduler uses host monotonic time and timers.
Pass the application’s monotonic scheduler when endpoint deadlines must share its clock. Omit it to use the host scheduler.
wallClock: Application IWallClock supplies only wire sentAt and hook timestamps as nonnegative safe-integer epoch milliseconds.
systemWallClock uses the host epoch clock.
Set a wall clock when wire timestamps and diagnostic timestamps must use the application clock. It does not control deadlines.
transport: Actual application adapter selected by top-level config or native connect middleware; native source evidence remains adapter-owned.
Absent: use the selected connect middleware transport; otherwise construction fails.
Supply the exact original carrier side owned by this caller; choose a transport factory for the supported host.
protocol: Canonical semantic IRpcProtocol descriptor selected independently of codec encoding.
rpcProtocolV1 is the default canonical protocol.
Use the protocol descriptor agreed by both ends. Omit it for Core’s default protocol.
codec: ICodec from @migaia/serialize/codec whose encoded output exactly matches the selected framer input.
identityCodecV1 preserves the canonical semantic envelope.
Use a codec whose output matches the framer input. Both ends must agree on the encoded representation.
framer: IRpcFramer from rpc-contract/framing whose actual output is accepted by the selected transport.
messageFramerV1 uses complete unfragmented messages.
Use the framer agreed by both ends; its output must match the transport’s accepted frame.
targetIds: Optional known-peer base identifiers from application deployment configuration; automatic discovery can resolve more later.
Empty seed list; discovery remains available.
provider: Application map of unique method names to IRpcProvider callbacks installed before endpoint construction returns.
Absent: register providers later through provide.
Register startup handlers here when they must exist before ingress starts. Later registrations can use provide on a provider-capable endpoint.
providerLimits: Optional IRpcProviderLimits applied to the existing shared execution/replay admission owner.
Global 256, per-peer 64, replay per-peer 1024.
Bound active provider work when expensive operations need backpressure. The defaults are 256 global and 64 per peer.
idempotency: Optional actual original result store and authenticated scope function for keyed provider work.
Absent: use the endpoint-owned canonical keyed replay policy.
Provide an outcome store on the serving endpoint when retries carry the same idempotency key. A shared store also needs a session scope.
idempotency.store: Optional caller-held IRpcIdempotencyStore shared only across actual intended sessions.
Absent: use the original endpoint-local store.
idempotency.scope: Synchronous application callback receives actual admitted token and senderId, returns a stable scope string; it must not treat arbitrary wire claims as identity.
Absent: canonical admitted-session scope is used.
Derive isolation from an admitted token when sharing an outcome store across sessions.
replay: Outbound active identifiers plus settled tombstone retention, separate from business result storage.
Use maxEntries 4096 and ttlMs 310000.
Size retained outbound identifiers for the request rate and replay window. This ledger is separate from the keyed business-result store.
replay.maxEntries: Maximum retained outbound request identities including active operations and settled tombstones.
`4096` retained outbound identities.
replay.ttlMs: Scheduler milliseconds to retain settled outbound request identity tombstones.
`310000` milliseconds after settlement.
middlewares: Required ordered finite tuple of actual middleware definitions installed atomically by PluginHost.
features: Optional finite immutable tuple of actual native IRpcFeature roots; dependencies remain private and only selected public surfaces are projected.
Empty tuple adds no user-defined features.
Install application features when endpoint-owned cleanup should release them. Omit this tuple when no extra feature is needed.
construction: Caller construction cancellation/deadline; failure still rolls back every installed middleware in original lifecycle order.
Absent: no caller abort or construction deadline.
construction.signal: Optional caller cancellation signal controlling construction and its complete rollback.
Absent: construction has an uncancelled native signal.
construction.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative construction deadline or false to disable; rollback retains the primary failure and cleanup failures.
Absent or false: no construction deadline.
Disable only the construction deadline.
Use false to rely solely on caller cancellation; use a finite budget when construction must finish within a deadline.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
orderKey: Application-issued ordering lane key; the final provider owns arrival ordering for equal keys.
Absent: no explicit ordering lane is requested.
cancel: Only before-start requests final-provider cancellation arbitration before execution begins.
Absent: ordinary cancellation keeps its existing owner.
The final provider decides cancellation before its actual execution start.
Choose before-start only when the final provider must decide cancellation before actual execution starts. Omission leaves ordinary cancellation with its existing owner. In capability calculation this mode adds cancel-before-start and excludes ordinary timeout/signal requirements.
timeoutMs: Optional finite nonnegative local deadline in milliseconds; false disables it. For scalar send, omission uses the installed timeout configuration: no plugin falls back to 1000 ms, while timeout({}) configures undefined and no local deadline. Ping and discovery queries have their own waiting defaults.
Scalar send inherits the installed timeout value; no plugin means 1000 ms, and timeout({}) means no deadline. Other operations use their documented waiting defaults.
Explicitly keep this operation unbounded by a local deadline.
idempotencyKey: Application-issued stable operation key reused only when requesting the same business effect.
Absent: no idempotency lookup or reservation is requested.
signal: Optional caller-owned AbortSignal; cancellation participates only when the required abort capability is installed.
Absent: no caller cancellation signal is attached.
transfer: Optional caller-supplied original transferable objects in the intended order; the real carrier validates support and ownership.
Absent: no ownership transfer is requested.

symbols.core:
signal: Optional caller-owned AbortSignal; cancellation participates only when the required abort capability is installed.
Absent: no caller cancellation signal is attached.
timeoutMs: Optional finite nonnegative local deadline in milliseconds; false disables it. For scalar send, omission uses the installed timeout configuration: no plugin falls back to 1000 ms, while timeout({}) configures undefined and no local deadline. Ping and discovery queries have their own waiting defaults.
Scalar send inherits the installed timeout value; no plugin means 1000 ms, and timeout({}) means no deadline. Other operations use their documented waiting defaults.
Explicitly keep this operation unbounded by a local deadline.
transfer: Optional caller-supplied original transferable objects in the intended order; the real carrier validates support and ownership.
Absent: no ownership transfer is requested.
idempotencyKey: Application-issued stable key reused only for the same intended operation; requires actual idempotency capability.
Absent: no keyed replay reservation.
trace: Optional caller-issued opaque diagnostic trace; downstream calls must pass it explicitly.
Absent: no trace is attached.

symbols.signature: export declare const RpcCoreErrorCode: { /** * A cold Probe listener, middleware installation callback, or diagnostic reporter throws. Forwarding rejects before * admission and sending; callers must choose a route that does not revisit a Host. */ readonly forwardLoop: 'FORWARD_LOOP'; /** * Three forwarding nodes have already been visited. Forwarding rejects a fourth before admission * and sending; callers may establish a direct connect/listen channel instead. */ readonly forwardHopLimit: 'FORWARD_HOP_LIMIT'; /** * Two middleware declarations in the same factory use the same `name`. * * The installer rejects before installing any middleware. The caller gives each middleware a * unique `name`. Enforces the duplicate singleton middleware creation rule. */ readonly middlewareDuplicated: 'MIDDLEWARE_DUPLICATED'; /** * An operation requires a capability that is not installed. * * Examples include creating an endpoint without `connect` or calling `ping()` without `ping`. * Remote abort notification additionally needs `abort`; local signal cancellation alone does not. * The caller installs the capability required by the intended operation. */ readonly middlewareMissing: 'MIDDLEWARE_MISSING'; /** * A Runtime API operation requires a mode or capability absent from the actual peer agreement. * Choose a supported method/mode rather than retrying the same operation. */ readonly capabilityUnsupported: 'CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED'; /** * A factory, middleware, or transport descriptor or configuration field is invalid. Replay * protection also rejects encrypt-only configuration, unavailable entropy, and exhausted * counters. * * This code identifies argument and configuration failures. The caller corrects the configuration * using `detail` before retrying. */ readonly invalidConfig: 'INVALID_CONFIG'; /** * A probe emit, describe or redact callback fails. Probe-core reports it with the original cause * and isolates it from business execution; callers should repair or disable the diagnostic sink. */ readonly probeFailed: 'PROBE_FAILED'; /** * `provide()` registers the same method twice. * * A provider does not replace another provider with the same name. The caller combines the * implementations or changes the name. */ readonly providerDuplicated: 'PROVIDER_DUPLICATED'; /** * A protocol codec, scheme, or envelope is invalid, the caller cannot reconstruct a response * error, or a provider receives an invalid abort payload. This is the base code for * `RpcProtocolError`. * * The caller checks that the protocol configuration matches the peer scheme. If the payload is * already sent or cancellation has taken effect, inspect the peer rather than retrying the same * message. */ readonly protocolInvalid: 'PROTOCOL_INVALID'; /** * Contract fields, direction, or request/response correlation are invalid. This is the base code * for `RpcContractError`. * * The caller checks `version`, `identifier`, sender/target direction, or `taskId`/method * correlation. */ readonly contractInvalid: 'CONTRACT_INVALID'; /** * A codec payload violates its input rules, or sender-side error serialization degrades a read or * data projection. This is the base code for `RpcSerializationError`. Physical batch * shape/encoding failures preserve the contract cause; malformed semantic members are reported * individually without discarding valid siblings. * * The caller checks the data, codec, or thrown value. Do not retry the same payload if it is * already sent or cancellation has taken effect. */ readonly payloadInvalid: 'PAYLOAD_INVALID'; /** * The provider executor cannot find a provider for the target method (`Provider not found`). * * The caller checks whether `provide()` registers the method. Do not retry the failed lookup. * This is the wire code for an inbound provider lookup failure. */ readonly providerNotFound: 'PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND'; /** * A non-dispatch provider does not return `ctx.success()` or `ctx.failed()`. * * The caller ensures every non-dispatch branch explicitly returns a result, or selects dispatch * if that is intended. */ readonly providerNotSettled: 'PROVIDER_NOT_SETTLED'; /** * A provider throws an unhandled exception. symbols.purpose: Stable semantic failure codes owned by the runtime-neutral Core execution layer. The stable values below select actual contract behavior; declarations alone grant no capability.
symbols.core:
providerGenerationMismatch: PROVIDER_GENERATION_MISMATCH: accepted caller/provider generation no longer matches the task; select the actual binding again.
providerGenerationRetired: PROVIDER_GENERATION_RETIRED: an admitted forwarded execution retired with its exact generation; never replay it.
forwardLoop: FORWARD_LOOP: signed route revisits this or the selected next Host; choose another route.
forwardHopLimit: FORWARD_HOP_LIMIT: three forwarding nodes were already visited; use a direct channel or shorter route.
middlewareDuplicated: MIDDLEWARE_DUPLICATED: names repeat in the construction tuple; assign one unique name per middleware.
middlewareMissing: MIDDLEWARE_MISSING: the operation requires an actually installed connect, abort, ping or other middleware capability.
capabilityUnsupported: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED: actual peer agreement does not support the requested runtime mode or capability.
invalidConfig: INVALID_CONFIG: factory, component, transport or transform configuration is invalid; inspect detail and correct local inputs.
probeFailed: PROBE_FAILED: a diagnostic emit/describe/redact callback failed; business execution remains isolated.
providerDuplicated: PROVIDER_DUPLICATED: provide registered a method that already has an owner; change the method or combine providers.
protocolInvalid: PROTOCOL_INVALID: codec/protocol/envelope behavior or correlated control is invalid; inspect original cause.
contractInvalid: CONTRACT_INVALID: method correlation, direction or contract identity fields violate the actual request contract.
payloadInvalid: PAYLOAD_INVALID: data, physical batch encoding or error projection violates its selected codec boundary.
providerNotFound: PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND: the receiving endpoint has no registered provider for the requested method.
providerNotSettled: PROVIDER_NOT_SETTLED: a request provider returned without an explicit success or failed result.
callbackFailed: CALLBACK_FAILED: a construction or diagnostic callback failed; native mutable errors retain type, stack and identity, foreign semantic identities stay unchanged, and other values remain on cause.
internal: INTERNAL: provider threw unexpectedly; original error stays in local diagnostics while the peer receives a redacted failure.
targetUnknown: TARGET_UNKNOWN: target or receiver is unresolved, inactive or outside the original selected binding.
targetNotIdentifiable: TARGET_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: anonymous broadcast group cannot satisfy a per-instance operation.
endpointDisposed: ENDPOINT_DISPOSED: an operation used a disposed endpoint; construct a new owner instead.
cancelled: CANCELLED: actual caller AbortSignal cancelled the local send; remote effects may already have occurred.
deadlineExceeded: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the local operation deadline expired; treat this transmission attempt as failed.
contextExpired: PROVIDER_CONTEXT_EXPIRED: success or failed was called after the original provider lifetime ended; no wire effect is produced.
transport: TRANSPORT: actual physical send or terminal channel failed; preserve original transport evidence before choosing recovery. The code alone never proves nonexecution; retry requires independent evidence or idempotency/outcome reconciliation.
authenticationFailed: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: signing, verification, encryption, decryption or original replay binding failed; details stay local.
schemaInvalid: SCHEMA_INVALID: params/result parse rejected the method data; inspect normalized issues and original cause.
capabilityConflict: CAPABILITY_CONFLICT: selected middleware/features publish conflicting keys or an ambiguous runtime instance.
overloaded: OVERLOADED: execution/replay/discovery/chunk capacity refused new work; inspect its independent reason channel.
streamResultUnknown: STREAM_RESULT_UNKNOWN: transport may have sent a stream frame before rejecting; open a new stream without replaying items.
chunkInvalid: CHUNK_INVALID: physical fragment grammar is invalid; hooks observe it and the frame is not replayed.
propertyReadFailed: PROPERTY_READ_FAILED: a getter/proxy failed without a valid synchronous reporter, or that reporter threw.
idempotencyResultUnavailable: IDEMPOTENCY_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE: business already ran but result was not retained; resolve outcome before another attempt.
stringConversionFailed: STRING_CONVERSION_FAILED: conversion or its required synchronous reporter failed; preserve original cause.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this const.

members.name: callbackFailed
members.description: A cold Probe listener, middleware installation callback, or diagnostic reporter throws. The * original remains reachable; callers repair the callback rather than retrying side effects.

members.name: providerGenerationMismatch
members.description: The selected authenticated provider/caller generation no longer matches this task; select * again.

members.name: providerGenerationRetired
members.description: Retires an admitted forward execution with its exact generation; never replay it.

members.name: forwardLoop
members.description: A signed route already contains this Host or the selected next Host. Forwarding rejects before * admission and sending; callers must choose a route that does not revisit a Host.

members.name: forwardHopLimit
members.description: Three forwarding nodes have already been visited. Forwarding rejects a fourth before admission * and sending; callers may establish a direct connect/listen channel instead.

members.name: middlewareDuplicated
members.description: Two middleware declarations in the same factory use the same `name`. * * The installer rejects before installing any middleware. The caller gives each middleware a * unique `name`. Enforces the duplicate singleton middleware creation rule.

members.name: middlewareMissing
members.description: An operation requires a capability that is not installed. * * Examples include creating an endpoint without `connect` or calling `ping()` without `ping`. * Remote abort notification additionally needs `abort`; local signal cancellation alone does not. * The caller installs the capability required by the intended operation.

members.name: capabilityUnsupported
members.description: A Runtime API operation requires a mode or capability absent from the actual peer agreement. * Choose a supported method/mode rather than retrying the same operation.

members.name: invalidConfig
members.description: A factory, middleware, or transport descriptor or configuration field is invalid. Replay * protection also rejects encrypt-only configuration, unavailable entropy, and exhausted * counters. * * This code identifies argument and configuration failures. The caller corrects the configuration * using `detail` before retrying.

members.name: probeFailed
members.description: A probe emit, describe or redact callback fails. Probe-core reports it with the original cause * and isolates it from business execution; callers should repair or disable the diagnostic sink.

members.name: providerDuplicated
members.description: `provide()` registers the same method twice. * * A provider does not replace another provider with the same name. The caller combines the * implementations or changes the name.

members.name: protocolInvalid
members.description: A protocol codec, scheme, or envelope is invalid, the caller cannot reconstruct a response * error, or a provider receives an invalid abort payload. This is the base code for * `RpcProtocolError`. * * The caller checks that the protocol configuration matches the peer scheme. If the payload is * already sent or cancellation has taken effect, inspect the peer rather than retrying the same * message.

members.name: contractInvalid
members.description: Contract fields, direction, or request/response correlation are invalid. This is the base code * for `RpcContractError`. * * The caller checks `version`, `identifier`, sender/target direction, or `taskId`/method * correlation.

members.name: payloadInvalid
members.description: A codec payload violates its input rules, or sender-side error serialization degrades a read or * data projection. This is the base code for `RpcSerializationError`. Physical batch * shape/encoding failures preserve the contract cause; malformed semantic members are reported * individually without discarding valid siblings. * * The caller checks the data, codec, or thrown value. Do not retry the same payload if it is * already sent or cancellation has taken effect.

members.name: providerNotFound
members.description: The provider executor cannot find a provider for the target method (`Provider not found`). * * The caller checks whether `provide()` registers the method. Do not retry the failed lookup. * This is the wire code for an inbound provider lookup failure.

members.name: providerNotSettled
members.description: A non-dispatch provider does not return `ctx.success()` or `ctx.failed()`. * * The caller ensures every non-dispatch branch explicitly returns a result, or selects dispatch * if that is intended.

members.name: internal
members.description: A provider throws an unhandled exception. This is the standard code for an `INTERNAL` response. * * Only local hooks receive the redacted original exception. The peer receives `RpcRemoteError` * with code `INTERNAL`.

members.name: targetUnknown
members.description: A target or receiver is unresolved, inactive, or outside the current binding. * * The caller checks whether `targetId` is registered or discovered, or whether `receiverSelector` * returns an unknown receiver.

members.name: targetNotIdentifiable
members.description: An operation requires an individual receiver, but the target is an anonymous BroadcastChannel * group. * * The caller configures `uniqueTargetId` and `identifier` before pinning, or avoids per-instance * operations on the group.

members.name: endpointDisposed
members.description: An endpoint operation runs after disposal (`RpcLifecycleError`). * * The caller creates a new endpoint instead of reusing the closed instance.

members.name: cancelled
members.description: The caller's `AbortSignal` cancels a local send (`RpcAbortError`). * * The caller handles this cooperative cancellation separately from remote failures.

members.name: deadlineExceeded
members.description: A local deadline expires (`RpcTimeoutError`). * * The caller checks target reachability and the timeout duration. Treat the request failure as * the result of this transmission attempt.

members.name: contextExpired
members.description: `ctx.success()` or `ctx.failed()` runs after the provider task ends. * * The expired result produces no wire effects. The caller keeps response logic within the * provider's synchronous or awaited lifetime.

members.name: transport
members.description: A transport send fails, a terminal event occurs, or the transport closes (`RpcTransportError`). * * The code alone does not establish whether a send already executed. Retry only with independent * evidence that it did not execute, or use the existing idempotency/outcome reconciliation.

members.name: authenticationFailed
members.description: A per-frame authentication transform fails during encryption, signing, verification, or * decryption (`RpcAuthenticationError`). Replay protection rejects missing/invalid binding, * duplicate counters and untrusted physical sessions. * * The caller checks key and algorithm configuration. Failure details are not sent back to the * peer.

members.name: schemaInvalid
members.description: Method parameters or results violate the contract schema (`RpcSchemaValidationError`). * * The caller corrects the data using `data.issues` rather than retrying the same invalid data.

members.name: capabilityConflict
members.description: A capability is published twice, or a frozen capability registry receives another write. Also * rejects folded Feature method collisions and ambiguous runtime instances. * * The caller checks middleware for duplicate declarations of reserved capabilities. This is a * configuration error.

members.name: overloaded
members.description: A local capacity limit rejects new work in provider admission, the replay ledger, discovery * waiters, outbound IDs, or chunks. * * The caller reduces concurrency, shortens TTL, or increases capacity. This signals backpressure * rather than a logic error.

members.name: streamResultUnknown
members.description: A stream frame may have been sent before its transport rejected; the caller must open a fresh * stream and never replay delivered values.

members.name: chunkInvalid
members.description: A chunk frame has an invalid format. This is the base code for `RpcChunkError`. * * The caller checks chunk configuration (`chunkSize` ≥ 4) and the peer implementation. An invalid * frame only invokes hooks and is not retried.

members.name: propertyReadFailed
members.description: A getter or Proxy throws during `safeRead` without a synchronous reporter, or the reporter * itself throws. The caller repairs the input or supplies a synchronous `report` at a boundary * that owns a diagnostic sink.

members.name: idempotencyResultUnavailable
members.description: A keyed call already executed but its result was not retained for replay. The caller must * resolve the outcome before issuing another non-idempotent attempt.

members.description: A string conversion throws without a synchronous reporter, or its reporter throws (cleanup ). * The caller must repair the input or provide a synchronous diagnostic sink.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Stable semantic failure codes owned by the runtime-neutral Core execution layer. The stable values below select actual contract behavior; declarations alone grant no capability.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import RpcCoreErrorCode from @migaia/rpc-core, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use RpcCoreErrorCode when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when RpcCoreErrorCode does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained const example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
providerGenerationMismatch: PROVIDER_GENERATION_MISMATCH: accepted caller/provider generation no longer matches the task; select the actual binding again.
providerGenerationRetired: PROVIDER_GENERATION_RETIRED: an admitted forwarded execution retired with its exact generation; never replay it.
forwardLoop: FORWARD_LOOP: signed route revisits this or the selected next Host; choose another route.
forwardHopLimit: FORWARD_HOP_LIMIT: three forwarding nodes were already visited; use a direct channel or shorter route.
middlewareDuplicated: MIDDLEWARE_DUPLICATED: names repeat in the construction tuple; assign one unique name per middleware.
middlewareMissing: MIDDLEWARE_MISSING: the operation requires an actually installed connect, abort, ping or other middleware capability.
capabilityUnsupported: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED: actual peer agreement does not support the requested runtime mode or capability.
invalidConfig: INVALID_CONFIG: factory, component, transport or transform configuration is invalid; inspect detail and correct local inputs.
probeFailed: PROBE_FAILED: a diagnostic emit/describe/redact callback failed; business execution remains isolated.
providerDuplicated: PROVIDER_DUPLICATED: provide registered a method that already has an owner; change the method or combine providers.
protocolInvalid: PROTOCOL_INVALID: codec/protocol/envelope behavior or correlated control is invalid; inspect original cause.
contractInvalid: CONTRACT_INVALID: method correlation, direction or contract identity fields violate the actual request contract.
payloadInvalid: PAYLOAD_INVALID: data, physical batch encoding or error projection violates its selected codec boundary.
providerNotFound: PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND: the receiving endpoint has no registered provider for the requested method.
providerNotSettled: PROVIDER_NOT_SETTLED: a request provider returned without an explicit success or failed result.
callbackFailed: CALLBACK_FAILED: a construction or diagnostic callback failed; native mutable errors retain type, stack and identity, foreign semantic identities stay unchanged, and other values remain on cause.
internal: INTERNAL: provider threw unexpectedly; original error stays in local diagnostics while the peer receives a redacted failure.
targetUnknown: TARGET_UNKNOWN: target or receiver is unresolved, inactive or outside the original selected binding.
targetNotIdentifiable: TARGET_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: anonymous broadcast group cannot satisfy a per-instance operation.
endpointDisposed: ENDPOINT_DISPOSED: an operation used a disposed endpoint; construct a new owner instead.
cancelled: CANCELLED: actual caller AbortSignal cancelled the local send; remote effects may already have occurred.
deadlineExceeded: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the local operation deadline expired; treat this transmission attempt as failed.
contextExpired: PROVIDER_CONTEXT_EXPIRED: success or failed was called after the original provider lifetime ended; no wire effect is produced.
transport: TRANSPORT: actual physical send or terminal channel failed; preserve original transport evidence before choosing recovery. The code alone never proves nonexecution; retry requires independent evidence or idempotency/outcome reconciliation.
authenticationFailed: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: signing, verification, encryption, decryption or original replay binding failed; details stay local.
schemaInvalid: SCHEMA_INVALID: params/result parse rejected the method data; inspect normalized issues and original cause.
capabilityConflict: CAPABILITY_CONFLICT: selected middleware/features publish conflicting keys or an ambiguous runtime instance.
overloaded: OVERLOADED: execution/replay/discovery/chunk capacity refused new work; inspect its independent reason channel.
streamResultUnknown: STREAM_RESULT_UNKNOWN: transport may have sent a stream frame before rejecting; open a new stream without replaying items.
chunkInvalid: CHUNK_INVALID: physical fragment grammar is invalid; hooks observe it and the frame is not replayed.
propertyReadFailed: PROPERTY_READ_FAILED: a getter/proxy failed without a valid synchronous reporter, or that reporter threw.
idempotencyResultUnavailable: IDEMPOTENCY_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE: business already ran but result was not retained; resolve outcome before another attempt.
stringConversionFailed: STRING_CONVERSION_FAILED: conversion or its required synchronous reporter failed; preserve original cause.

blocks.text: 错误保留原生类型、message、stack 与 cause；错误形状用 IRpcError，平台/拓扑值域用 IRpcPlatformValue / IRpcTransportTopologyValue。按稳定 source/code 而非 message 分支，远端身份只作诊断，不授予本地控制权。

isRpcErrorInstance / isRpcRemoteError / isRpcTimeoutError 按稳定字段跨 realm/副本判断，不能依赖 instanceof；isRpcError 只检查字符串 code，不能替代错误族守卫。RpcError、RpcRemoteError、RpcTimeoutError 等仅类型导出，唯一公开可构造类为 RpcLifecycleError，供持有自身释放状态的消费方使用。

symbols.purpose:
Installs a local deadline default resolved per operation, retaining explicit false to disable a particular wait.

The examples use application-chosen id values and a caller-created memory transport pair. Both transport and connect({ transport }) refer to the same side; memory options default to {}, with asynchronous delivery and no value cloning. middlewares is the required installation tuple; targetIds is an optional application seed list, default []. provide registers an application method whose context.data is the request and context.success(value) forms its reply. send(targetId, method, data, options?) takes the target and method named by that application; options defaults to {}. Dispose each endpoint, then close the borrowed pair as its creator.
symbols.core:
config: Application configuration documented by IRpcTimeoutConfig; factory returns a definition, installation occurs in createEndpoint middlewares.
Immutable IRpcPlugin definition; unsupported or unreadable fields fail the original installation with INVALID_CONFIG and retained cause.
timeoutMs: Optional finite nonnegative default deadline in milliseconds; false disables local default deadlines.
Omitted timeoutMs in timeout({}) stays undefined and sets no local deadline; omitting the plugin entirely uses Core fallback 1000 ms.
Explicitly keep this operation unbounded by a local deadline.
Choose finite milliseconds for bounded waits or false when the application deliberately owns the waiting lifetime.
Installs the original timeout capability into one canonical endpoint construction transaction; it has no standalone network effect.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
report: Synchronous callback receives background or contained failures as error; no return is consumed, and failure handling stays with the original runtime reporter owner.
report.error: Original background or secondary failure supplied by the runtime owner.
No result is used; reporter errors are contained by the reporting boundary.
Omitted: defaultRpcReporter reports to console.error.
keyFactory: Advanced remote-proxy key callback returning an application string for automatically keyed retry paths. The direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read this inherited field itself.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.
retryPort: Advanced application-supplied retry dispatch port for remote-proxy paths; it receives the original retry input and returns the selected dispatch result. Direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read it itself.
Omitted: the remote proxy keeps its original retry dispatch owner; no second retry policy is installed by a direct peer.
spawn: Application physical input issued by its deployment launcher; selects this definition launch operation.
Absent: no launch source.
connect: Application physical input issued by its connection owner; selects this definition open/dial operation.
Absent: no connect source.
listen: Application physical input issued by its listener owner; selects this definition listening operation.
Absent: no listener source.
peerId: Actual remote identifier learned by the deployment owner; message adapters may learn it through their original initial exchange.
Absent: message exchange may learn the address; byte construction requires its actual address.
scheduler: Application monotonic IScheduler shared by the original connection owners.
systemScheduler uses native time and timers.
offer: Local rpc-contract IRpcHandshakeOffer proposal; received I/O determines accepted capabilities.
Absent: Core compiles its canonical local offer.
auth: Actual responder verifier configuration; required mode receives portable credentials and admitted peer, returns principal string or void synchronously/asynchronously. Throws reject authentication.
Absent: no explicit responder verifier.
ipc: Actual connection/session diagnostic labels, capacities and local log sink chosen by the physical owner.
Absent: original Core connection defaults apply.
governor: Actual original connection policy for call-rate, payload, repeated-timeout, idle and violation limits; it borrows original provider admission.
Absent: no extra connection governor.
scope: Genuine scope returned by this adapter scope method; borrowed across peers and closed by its caller after peers close.
Absent: no caller-shared provider scope.
name: Caller-selected nonempty registration name copied when constructing the cold plugin; use the same name when addressing the installed runtime outlet.
expose: Distinct nonempty paths explicitly exposing current Host feature methods, runtime connection routes or the reserved host control entry. Only this snapshotted whitelist becomes remotely callable.
Omitted: an empty whitelist; only provide methods are published.
host: The same actual PluginHost handle into which this plugin is installed, supplying use, unUse, plugin and revision for explicit host exposure.
Omitted: allowed unless expose contains host; explicit host exposure requires host, catalog and resolvePlugin together.
catalog: Application-authored IRemoteHostCatalog declaring the only plugin contracts available through explicitly exposed host control.
Omitted: no host-control catalog; required when expose contains host.
resolvePlugin: Synchronous local resolver invoked by the canonical host-control owner after catalog admission; definitions remain local and are installed through the original Host.
resolvePlugin.name: Plugin name admitted by the declared catalog.
resolvePlugin.config: Optional portable configuration from the remote host-use request.
Local plugin definition accepted by the Host; a thrown error rejects the host-use request.
Omitted: no local resolver; required when expose contains host.

Readonly pair of borrowed, exclusive Memory transports; caller owns final pair close. No native transfer is performed.

examples:
import { connect, createEndpoint } from '@migaia/rpc-core'
import { createMemoryTransportPair } from '@migaia/rpc-core/adapters/memory'

const [left, right] = createMemoryTransportPair()
const server = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'server',
  transport: right,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: right })]
})
server.provide('double', (context) => context.success((context.data as number) * 2))
const client = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'client',
  targetIds: ['server'],
  transport: left,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: left })]
})
console.log(await client.send<number>('server', 'double', 21))
await client.dispose()
await server.dispose()
left.close()

import { connect, createEndpoint } from '@migaia/rpc-core'
import { createMemoryTransportPair } from '@migaia/rpc-core/adapters/memory'

const [left, right] = createMemoryTransportPair()
const endpoint = await createEndpoint({
  id: 'local',
  transport: left,
  middlewares: [connect({ transport: left })]
})
await endpoint.dispose()

declaredConfiguration.description: Initial provider methods registered before endpoint construction completes.

declaredConfiguration.description: Optional store and session scope used only for keyed provider requests.

declaredConfiguration.description: Borrowed store for keyed provider executions; omission selects the endpoint-owned default.

declaredConfiguration.type: (admission: Readonly<{ token: string; senderId: string; }>) => string
declaredConfiguration.description: Compute an authenticated deduplication namespace from admitted token and sender identity.

symbols.name: IOutboundSurface
symbols.signature: export type IOutboundSurface = Pick<IRpcEndpoint, 'send' | 'sendAll' | 'dispatch' | 'dispatchAll' | 'group' | 'outcome' | 'hooks'>;
symbols.purpose: Selected outbound projection contains requests, fanout, dispatch, group/outcome and local hooks without provider or discovery controls.
symbols.core:
send: Sends a correlated scalar request to the selected receiver and waits for one actual provider result.
send.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
send.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
send.data: Application request payload validated by the installed contract/codec.
send.options: Optional ISendOptions supplied by the caller; timeout, cancellation, transfer, idempotency and trace remain explicit.
Promise of provider data; remote business failure, cancellation, deadline, transport or lifecycle failure rejects with its native coded error. A synchronous UUID admission failure releases operation signal listeners; ordinary send cancellation keeps RpcAbortError.
sendAll: Sends the same scalar method to the statically configured target seeds and keeps each target success/failure separately.
sendAll.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
sendAll.data: Application payload sent independently to every selected target.
sendAll.options: Caller ISendOptions applied to the selected fan-out operations.
IRpcFanoutResult maps receiver/target keys to fulfilled data or original rejected errors.
dispatch: Sends a legacy one-way event without awaiting business completion; pair with on on the receiving endpoint.
dispatch.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
dispatch.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
dispatch.data: Application event payload for the receiving listener.
Returns void once dispatch is initiated; failures are contained in endpoint hooks.
dispatchAll: Dispatches one event to the statically configured target seeds without waiting for business listeners.
dispatchAll.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
dispatchAll.data: Application event payload for each selected target.
Returns void after scheduling selected dispatches; hooks observe failures.
group: Reserves every request-only step before execution, then runs in order until first failure; successful earlier effects are not rolled back.
group.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
group.steps: Application nonempty method/payload array admitted as IRpcRuntimeGroupSteps.
group.options: Optional IRpcRuntimeGroupOptions with actual ordering/cancellation/idempotency and local send controls.
Promise of actual step outcomes; unsupported native group capability rejects before dispatch.
outcome: Reads an original logical key outcome from the provider store without executing providers again.
outcome.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
outcome.idempotencyKey: Original application-issued key used for the same earlier logical operation.
IRpcRuntimeOutcomeResult reports pending/done/unknown and store continuity; unknown never proves nonexecution.
hooks: Local diagnostic subscription facade; hooks.on receives IRpcHookEvent and returns an unsubscriber.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Creates the full canonical endpoint preset through the same kernel and lifecycle as createEndpoint; feature dependencies remain privately installed.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import createFullEndpoint from @migaia/rpc-core/full, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use createFullEndpoint when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when createFullEndpoint does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained const example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

on.event: Application event name matching the sender dispatch method.

send: Sends a correlated scalar request to the selected receiver and waits for one actual provider result.

sendAll: Sends the same scalar method to the statically configured target seeds and keeps each target success/failure separately.
sendAll.method: Application method name registered by the receiving endpoint provide or declared in the actual remote contract.
sendAll.data: Application payload sent independently to every selected target.
sendAll.options: Caller ISendOptions applied to the selected fan-out operations.

group.targetId: Target base identifier selected by the application in targetIds or returned by endpoint discovery/server-list metadata.
